responsiveness.name: V1 Kaiser-PCA (single-std, eigenvalue>1)
responsiveness.note: Single static standardization (StandardScaler fit on TRAIN=2019-12-31) + PCA fit on the same train slice, projected to full history. Kaiser eigenvalue>1 retention. composite = raw PC1 (unit-variance, NO rolling re-z). Removes production's rolling-3y-z on features AND rolling-3y-z on PC1 (the triple-normalization lag). PC2 eigenvalue 0.665 <= 1 (Kaiser): only PC1 retained. raw_cov sub-variant: PCA on the UNSCALED covariance of the same levels is dominated by the largest-variance series (lev_money, raw var >> others), which is why standardization matters; reported in meta only, never the composite.

responsiveness.name: V2 CFTC/Street best-practice (COT-index + %OI + flow)
responsiveness.note: inp.buyside_level() is already DV01 / 10y-equivalent weighted (aggregate lev+AM net DV01, $mm/bp) per the OFR convention, so this IS a DV01-weighted COT index — not a raw-contract COT index.

responsiveness.name: V4 Curve (book-tilt vs momentum, PC2)
responsiveness.note: Two-dimension curve read: the RAW book tilt is ~flat (book_tilt ~ -5.18 $mm/bp) while MOMENTUM (EWMA-z hl=26) reads steepener-direction (+1.42). The raw book being ~flat and the momentum reading steepener are not in conflict: momentum measures drift vs recent history, not the absolute level. composite/curve = momentum; POSITIVE = crowded steepener.

responsiveness.name: V5 Kalman (deviation-σ / slope / acceleration)
responsiveness.note: Local-linear-trend Kalman on source=v0 (auto); headline=deviation. deviation>0 = above fair value (crowding building), slope>0 = positioning rising, acceleration>0 = accelerating.
